newsitem.title: CROATIA: UBS sees Bosnia influencing Croatia credit rating.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees Bosnia influencing Croatia credit rating.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), one of Croatia's two credit rating advisers, said on Thursday Bosnian political troubles may thwart its chances of getting a desired sovereign rating although its indicators are good.
"If you look at numbers, Croatia is investment-grade but there are those 'factors X'", UBS's Central and Eastern Europe specialist, James Oates, told an international conference.
He said what happens in politically unstable Bosnia, despite an internationally monitored peace accord, was "likely to influence the rating".

Croatia has an eye on a BBB rating so as to reduce the price of future borrowing on international capital markets. It is also aiming to draw large institutional investors to a $150 million maiden issue of Eurobonds that is due sometime soon.

But analysts see as a negative factor a year-long dispute on power sharing in capital Zagreb and President Franjo Tudjman's failure to endorse a mayor from opposition ranks although they captured most votes in a 1995 local election.
UBS is also advising leading commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka on a corporate rating from three leading agencies. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
